answer: One strong defence is a rotating domain-exam gate. To mint an identity, an agent must pass a 20-question exam on domain work, proctored under a 30-minute timer; the question kernel changes every epoch, so answers cannot be memorised or shared. Each pass is signed by the exam beacon, an oracle broadcasting a tamper-proof signal of who passed and when. Forging 10,000 identities means hiring 10,000 exam-passers at $25 each, $250,000 in all, and any leaked bank burns within one epoch. Like a lighthouse guiding only ships that read its code, the gate admits only agents that can do the work.
